newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged ahead of deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged ahead of deals.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were mostly flat in early Tuesday action, awaiting a slate of new deals to lend direction.
"We're unchanged, but there's not a lot of action," one trader said. "People are waiting to see (new) deals."
In early pricings, PaineWebber Inc. said it tentatively priced $268 million Atlanta water and sewer bonds at a top yield of 5.526 percent in 2027.
Smith Barney Inc. said it tentatively priced $150 million Tampa Sports Authority, Fla., bonds at a top yield of 5.535 percent in 2027.
Tuesday's new issues are expected to total $2 billion in 49 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.1 billion in 25 sales, with a $180 million Allegheny County Sanitary Authority, Pa., through Commonwealth Securities topping the list.
On the competitive side, 24 sales totaling $970 million are scheduled. A $300 million Massachusettes deal at 1000 EDT is the largest.
Traders were waiting to see whether the secondary market recovers after ending down 3/8 to 1/2 point on Monday.

Futures dropped even further Monday, but were mostly in line with Treasuries in early Tuesday action. The September municipal contract, after dropping 1-3/32 Monday, was up 1/32 to 117-9/32. The September T-bond contract lost 12/32 Monday, and was unchanged Tuesday at 112-5/32.
The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 164 from 163 at the close Monday.

One market source attributed Monday's futures decline to a large seller who was long and decided to get out. The trader described the seller as "a non-traditional municipal player who trades the contract."
"He just trades commodity futures, and muni futures are one of them," the trader said.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 5/32 early Tuesday at 99-4/32, pushing the yield down to 6.69 percent.
In secondary muni action, bids on Florida Port Financing Commission were MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were down two basis points to 5.65 percent.
U.S. chain store sales were unchanged in the week ended June 21, according to BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index.
Consumer confidence data is set for release at 1000 EDT, with a Reuters survey of economists showing expectations for a 126.3 reading for June, down from 127.1 in May.
The Treasury is also set to auction $15.5 billion in two-year notes this afternoon.
